atoms.definition:
This module is a VGA vertical (frame) timing counter: it counts on a single clock and outputs the current count, four phase flags
(visible region, front porch, sync pulse phase, back porch), and a last-line flag. The phase flags are mutually exclusive and exhaustive over counts 0..524.
The module contains no pixel or horizontal timing logic, nor any external registers or bus interface; thresholds are fixed constants.
OutSP is an active-high sync pulse phase indicator, and the module has no separate port that performs polarity conversion.
Upstream provides Clock, Reset, and Enabled; downstream consumes OutCounter and the flags. The module has no subinstances,
queues, storage arrays, or arbiters, and there are no cross-module reset or arbitration semantics.
atoms.title: Role and Boundaries

atoms.definition:
There are 9 ports in total: Clock, Reset, and Enabled are inputs; OutVisible, OutFP, OutSP, OutBP, and OutMax
are 1-bit outputs; OutCounter is a 10-bit unsigned output ([9:0]).
- Clock is the only clock; the running count state updates only on Clock rising edges.
- Reset is a synchronous, active-high reset sampled only on Clock rising edges. Changing Reset between edges does not immediately load the count;
  a reset pulse entirely between two rising edges does not change the count. There is no combinational gating to force outputs during reset.
- Enabled is sampled on Clock rising edges; when Reset is 0, Enabled being 1 advances the count, and being 0 holds it.
- Outputs are combinational, with no output registers: outputs are in phase with OutCounter and reflect the new count immediately after the clock
  edge. Here, “after the edge” means a stable observation point after both the nonblocking state update and combinational propagation have completed;
  it does not mean that the new state can already be read in the rising-edge active region, before the NBA update.
The module has no ready/valid handshake, backpressure, or cancellation; input acceptance conditions are determined by Clock rising edges and Reset/Enabled.
atoms.title: Interface Contract

atoms.definition:
The count state is a 10-bit unsigned number. At each Clock rising edge, it updates with the following priority:
- When Reset == 1, load 1, meaning the count after reset is 1 (not 0), regardless of whether Enabled is 0 or 1.
- When Reset == 0 and Enabled == 1, if the current count is 524, the next state is 0; otherwise, add 1.
- When Reset == 0 and Enabled == 0, hold the current count.
After a sampled reset establishes the state, legal input histories keep the count within 0..524, with a cycle length of 525.
The first cycle established by reset starts at 1; the first enabled rising edge after reset release advances 1 to 2.
The register declaration in the fixed RTL also has an initial value of 0: after HDL simulation initialization and combinational settling, before the first rising edge,
OutCounter=0 can be observed. This declaration initial value is not equal to the synchronous reset value and does not guarantee the power-up state of physical hardware without reset.
For state preparation and the valid domain for runtime checks in this problem, see R-VGA-005.
atoms.title: Vertical count

atoms.definition:
Combinational decoding directly uses the current OutCounter, with thresholds 480, 490, 492, and 525, and a last-line value of 524:
- OutVisible is 1 if and only if the count is less than 480: within the legal domain, 0..479, totaling 480 counts.
- OutFP is 1 if and only if 480 <= count < 490: 480..489, totaling 10 counts.
- OutSP is 1 if and only if 490 <= count < 492: 490..491, totaling 2 counts.
- OutBP is 1 if and only if 492 <= count < 525: 492..524, totaling 33 counts.
- OutMax is 1 if and only if the count equals 524.
When a flag's condition is not satisfied, that flag is 0. The four phase lengths sum to 525, and count 0 belongs to the visible region.
OutMax and OutBP may simultaneously be 1; the mutual-exclusion requirement for the four phases does not include OutMax.
10 bits can represent values up to 1023, but the normal cycle explicitly wraps at 524 rather than relying on bit-width overflow.
atoms.title: Phase boundaries

atoms.definition:
Runtime verification uses Reset=1 sampled by at least one Clock rising edge as state preparation; native inputs are then used to advance or hold,
producing reachable counts of 0..524. Reset and Enabled use definite 0/1 levels, established before the rising edge and held
stable during sampling to avoid races between input driving and state sampling. Output checks must be performed after the NBA update and combinational logic
have settled at the rising edge of interest; values observed before the edge or before NBA still belong to the pre-update state and must not be treated as post-update values for the same edge.
Inter-edge reset behavior may be observed after combinational settling following an input change, and distinguished from the reset effect at the next sampling edge.
X/Z inputs, forced internal states, and counts 525..1023 are outside the runtime domain required for coverage in this problem; the delta
propagation process at initialization is also not an output comparison window. The simulation fact of the pre-reset declaration initial value cannot replace the state preparation above.
